title: Fare Thee Honey Blues — Mamie Smith & Her Jazz Hounds (1920)
lyrics:
My baby has left me, I don't know what I'll do
Now every day I've been here, it makes me feel so blue
I'm leaving here today, and that is why

I'm leaving town to wear you off my mind
I've been mistreated and I don't mind dying
I'll buy me a ticket as long as my right arm
I'll ride so far you'll think I'm dead and gone

I'll find me a man, just as long as I'm home
If you don't want me, why don't you tell me so

I can get a friend most anywhere I go
There's a place in Georgia, a change is in the middle of me
I don't want nobody that don't want me
Don't you leave me here
direction: A rented room and a small-town railway station, 1920, late afternoon into dusk; hand-tinted 35mm, no modern objects

treatment.title_treatment: I’ll keep us inside a rented room and a small-town railway station in 1920, carrying late afternoon into dusk through hand-tinted 35mm, tobacco gold, faded rose and gathering blue. An invented woman turns abandonment into the practical work of leaving; restrained camera moves and stubborn little gestures answer the blues, with no modern objects, readable markings, on-screen text or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 1, instrumental opening
cues.cue: Bar 1 opens on the rented room; include the opening lead-in and hold through bar 3.
cues.shot: Wide, slowly advancing view of a rented room in 1920 late afternoon: an invented woman in a plain period dress sits beside an empty chair, her face turned away. Hand-tinted 35mm in tobacco gold, window light crossing worn floorboards; only unmarked period objects and no text.

cues.anchor: Bar 4, opening instrumental phrase
cues.cue: Bar 4 turns to the empty chair for two bars.
cues.shot: In the same 1920 rented room at late afternoon, track sideways at table height past two cups toward one empty chair as the woman's hand removes the unused cup. Hand-tinted 35mm, faded rose shadows and soft window light; unmarked period furnishings, no text or facial close-up.

cues.anchor: Bar 6, loudness lift from 0.37 to 0.54
cues.cue: The bar 6 lift takes us to the station for four bars.
cues.shot: A small-town railway station in 1920 late afternoon, seen in a low lateral dolly along an empty wooden platform toward rails and a distant stationary steam locomotive. Hand-tinted 35mm, slanting tobacco-gold sunlight, entirely unmarked period architecture and equipment with no signs, numbers or text.

cues.anchor: Bar 6, first substantial instrumental lift
cues.cue: At the bar 6 lift, breathe the station's reflected sunlight once per beat for four bars.

cues.anchor: Bar 10, loudness recovery from 0.36 to 0.45
cues.cue: Bar 10 returns to the room; let the open suitcase wait for four bars.
cues.shot: In the rented room in 1920 late afternoon, a restrained overhead drift reveals an open, unlabelled leather suitcase and the woman's hands hovering above folded clothes. Hand-tinted 35mm, warm window light and dusty violet shadows, only period objects, no text or faces in close-up.

cues.cue: At bar 14, “My baby has left me” lands; hold her beside the untouched half of the bed for four bars.
cues.shot: Medium-wide rear view of the invented woman in the 1920 rented room at late afternoon, smoothing only one side of a narrow bed before her hand stops. A barely perceptible push-in, hand-tinted 35mm and faded rose window light preserve the empty space; period objects only, no text or facial close-up.

cues.anchor: Bar 18, “Now every day I've been here” and loudness jump to 0.51
cues.cue: Bar 18 brings “Now every day I've been here”; circle her repeated packing gesture for four bars.
cues.shot: In the 1920 rented room under lengthening late-afternoon light, the woman folds a blouse, unfolds it and finally lays it in her suitcase. A slow waist-height arc keeps her head out of frame; hand-tinted 35mm, muted blue-violet shadows, unmarked period belongings and no text.

cues.anchor: Bar 18, vocal line and loudness lift
cues.cue: At bar 18, cool the room's shadow side over four bars without dimming the afternoon window.

cues.anchor: Bar 22, “I'm leaving here today, and that is why”
cues.cue: On bar 22's “I'm leaving here today,” she shuts the case; follow her decision for four bars.
cues.shot: Low medium shot in the 1920 rented room at late afternoon: the woman closes the unlabelled leather suitcase, fastens its buckles and rises into the window light. Tilt only from her hands to her shoulders, hand-tinted 35mm with tobacco-gold highlights; no modern objects, text or facial close-up.

cues.anchor: Bar 26, landing of “I'm leaving town to wear you off my mind”
cues.cue: Bar 26 carries “I'm leaving town”; meet her suitcase at the station for four bars.
cues.shot: At the small-town railway station in 1920 late afternoon, track backward at knee height as the same woman carries her unlabelled suitcase along the wooden platform. Hand-tinted 35mm, long amber shadows and a plain period skirt moving against her stride; no signage, markings, modern objects or facial close-up.

cues.anchor: Bar 30, approach to “I've been mistreated and I don't mind dying”
cues.cue: Bar 30 approaches “I've been mistreated”; keep her upright and still on the station bench for four bars.
cues.shot: Medium-wide locked view of the woman sitting rigidly on a bench at the small-town railway station in 1920 late afternoon, suitcase braced between her shoes, hands gradually unclenching. Hand-tinted 35mm, faded rose light and violet shade; period setting without text, facial close-ups or literal images of death.

Hand-tinted 35mm and warm sidelight, both figures framed below the shoulders, all paper and surfaces blank to camera with no modern objects or text.

cues.anchor: Bar 38, loudness dip from 0.48 to 0.32
cues.cue: At bar 38's dip, hold the ticket hidden in her palm for three bars.
cues.shot: In the 1920 small-town railway station under waning late-afternoon light, a close detail of the woman's gloved hand closes around a face-down ticket beside her plain suitcase. A gentle downward camera drift, hand-tinted 35mm and violet wood-grain shadows; no faces, readable markings, text or modern objects.

cues.anchor: Bar 41, loudness lift to 0.55

Slowly pull back through the station doorway, hand-tinted 35mm, pale gold steam and blue-violet distance; no text or modern objects.

cues.anchor: Bar 44, loudness peak of 0.63
cues.cue: At bar 44's peak, broaden the gold backlight through the steam for three bars.

cues.anchor: Bar 47, loudness rebound to 0.56
cues.cue: Bar 47 rebounds; let her heel answer the rhythm for four bars.
cues.shot: Low tracking detail along the bench at the small-town railway station in 1920, late afternoon slipping toward dusk: the woman's buttoned boot taps lightly beside her suitcase. Hand-tinted 35mm, warm light raking the boards and cool shade beneath the bench; no lettering, modern objects or faces.

cues.anchor: Bar 51, loudness lift to 0.55
cues.cue: Bar 51 lifts; she squares her hat in the station window for two bars.
cues.shot: Medium rear view of the woman adjusting her plain period hat in an unlettered window at the small-town railway station in 1920, approaching dusk. A small forward glide keeps her reflection distant and indistinct; hand-tinted 35mm, faded rose highlights, period objects only and no text or facial close-up.

cues.anchor: Bar 53, response to “I'll find me a man, just as long as I'm home”
cues.cue: Bar 53 answers “I'll find me a man”; give her room to choose her own seat for four bars.
cues.shot: At the small-town railway station in 1920 near dusk, the woman deliberately moves her suitcase from the bench and settles into a more relaxed posture while a distant period traveller passes. Slowly widen the medium shot, hand-tinted 35mm with rose-tinted residual sunlight; no modern objects, signs, text or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 57, continuation of “If you don't want me, why don't you tell me so”
cues.cue: Bar 57 carries “If you don't want me”; return to the room she has emptied for four bars.
cues.shot: The rented room in 1920 near dusk stands empty, its suitcase gone and a single chair tucked neatly under the table. Repeat the opening's slow forward move on hand-tinted 35mm, now with blue-violet window light and a thin amber edge; unmarked period furnishings only, no text.

cues.anchor: Bar 61, loudness trough of 0.28
cues.cue: At bar 61's trough, watch the station lamps take over for four bars.
cues.shot: At the small-town railway station in 1920 dusk, a period attendant lights an unmarked oil platform lamp while the woman waits several paces behind. A slow upward tilt from the lamp base to its sheltered flame, hand-tinted 35mm, tobacco-gold practical light against blue dusk; no modern objects, text or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 61, quieter passage at 0.28
cues.cue: From bar 61, settle the station into a four-bar dusk-blue wash, preserving the warm oil lamps.

cues.anchor: Bar 65, approach to “I can get a friend most anywhere I go”

The departing woman acknowledges her with a small nod; hand-tinted 35mm, amber oil-lamp light, no text, modern objects or facial close-ups.

cues.anchor: Bar 67, loudness peak of 0.63
cues.cue: Bar 67 peaks; cut to her hand taking the suitcase for one bar.
cues.shot: A tight hand-and-case detail at the small-town railway station in 1920 dusk catches the woman firmly lifting her unlabelled leather suitcase. A brief rising camera movement on hand-tinted 35mm, amber oil-lamp edge light and deep blue shadows; no faces, text or modern objects.

cues.anchor: Bar 69, rebound to 0.51 and landing of “There's a place in Georgia”

The camera remains still outside, hand-tinted 35mm with amber interior light and dark blue steam; no markings, text or modern objects.

cues.anchor: Bar 78, last substantial loudness lift

Hand-tinted 35mm, deep dusk blue and a small tobacco-gold flame, no modern objects, signs, numbers or text.
